To estimate the wavelength of the photon emitted during a transition from \( n=3 \) to \( n=2 \) in a Fe atom (Z=26), we use the fact that the energy levels scale as \( Z^2 \). The energy levels are modeled as \( E_n = -\frac{Z^2 \cdot 13.6 \, \text{eV}}{n^2} \), where \( 13.6 \, \text{eV} \) is the ground-state energy of hydrogen.

### Energy Difference Calculation
The energy of the photon emitted is the difference between the two levels:
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = E_3 - E_2 = \left(-\frac{26^2 \cdot 13.6}{3^2}\right) - \left(-\frac{26^2 \cdot 13.6}{2^2}\right)
\]
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = 26^2 \cdot 13.6 \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{3^2}\right)
\]
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = 676 \cdot 13.6 \cdot \left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right)
\]
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = 676 \cdot 13.6 \cdot \frac{5}{36}
\]
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = 676 \cdot 13.6 \cdot 0.1389 \approx 1276.89 \, \text{eV}
\]

\[
\lambda = \frac{hc}{E_{\text{photon}}}
\]
where \( h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J·s} \) and \( c = 3.00 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \). Converting \( E_{\text{photon}} \) to joules:
\[
E_{\text{photon}} = 1276.89 \, \text{eV} \cdot 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{J/eV} \approx 2.045 \times 10^{-16} \, \text{J}
\]

\[
